name: West Papua
summary_text: West Papua shares the same security-force pattern documented for Papua province: 138 recorded acts of torture or ill-treatment in detention by police and military (Sep 2021–Q1 2025) with near-total impunity, arbitrary airport detentions, expanded military deployments, and forced displacement through Q3 2025. No trans-specific incident series was identified. The risk to a trans visitor is amplification of any police contact into unlawful detention and physical violence at rates far exceeding the national norm. Deviation from the national score (0.15) is −0.04. Like Papua, this is classified as a systemic-contact amplifier rather than a targeted-trans finding. The dossier explicitly notes the absence of trans-specific incidents while confirming that the probability of escalation during state contact is documented and elevated. West Papua's 2022 split from Papua means the same security apparatus operates under the same impunity conditions in the western portion of the island. West Papua scores identically to Papua (0.11) and sits below the enacted-regulatory provinces West Sumatra (0.12) and South Sulawesi (0.12), where the risk is administrative or legislative rather than physical-state violence, and below Jakarta (0.12), where police overreach drew strong rights-group condemnation.

sources.claim_summary: Asia-Pacific Solidarity / TAPOL briefing (22 Jul 2025), 'Torture in detention in West Papua: Impunity, secrecy and silence': documents 138 recorded acts of torture or ill-treatment in police and military detention in Maybrat and the Central Highlands between Sep 2021 and Q1 2025 with almost no accountability; victims mostly detained for alleged ties to armed groups or for protesting, deaths in custody recorded, and every case tracked in the 'Papuans Behind Bars' database — including arbitrary airport stops.

sources.title: Papua Quarterly Report Q3 2025: Violence and Impunity: Killings and arrests as security forces expand across West Papua -
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Monitor Papua quarterly report for Q3 2025 (Jul-Sep): documents sharply increased military deployments in the central highlands from August 2025, continued fatal shootings and arbitrary detentions, internal displacement, and the failure of accountability mechanisms — supporting the West Papua amplifier finding.
